title: The Perils and Promise of Relationships
coreMove: Pair openness with verification so trust grows at the speed of evidence rather than the speed of good feeling.
sourcePressure: The ch08 source closes on trust, truth bias, online deception, and guarded optimism. It must preserve both relationship promise and risk without collapsing into cynicism or naive warmth.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the warning into total suspicion, or treating warm signals and polished online presentation as proof.

sourceAnchors.name: truth bias
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch08 sidecar names truth bias as a risk because people default toward believing socially coherent signals.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Truth bias keeps normal life moving, but it becomes expensive when a polished signal is not backed by reality.

sourceAnchors.name: online misrepresentation
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says online presentation can separate surface signals from underlying reality and deserves more verification.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A profile can feel coherent before anything meaningful has been checked; that is where trust needs to slow down.

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator considering a large online commission from a charming new client
exampleSpecs.audience: a creator balancing opportunity with payment risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: two weeks of unpaid work could wipe out rent money
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the illustrator slows trust by requiring a deposit and checking the business record even though the client feels warm and urgent
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a color palette open beside an unsigned contract

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent evaluating a private online tutor for a teenager
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent who wants help without handing over trust too quickly
exampleSpecs.stakes: a child will spend unsupervised video hours with a stranger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What evidence matters more than the tutor profile: references, trial boundaries, or the speed of the friendly messages?

exampleSpecs.domain: a remote nonprofit board vetting a volunteer treasurer met through a forum
exampleSpecs.audience: a board chair tempted by competence signals
exampleSpecs.stakes: bank access could expose donor funds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "He sounds perfect," Anna says, then separates signal from evidence by asking what has actually been verified before access is granted

exampleSpecs.domain: a community language app user invited to move a conversation off-platform
exampleSpecs.audience: a user practicing guarded optimism without shutting down connection
exampleSpecs.stakes: the relationship could be real, but the new channel removes safeguards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you keep the conversation warm while asking for slower steps and platform boundaries until claims and behavior align
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blinking off-platform invitation under a translation prompt

exampleSpecs.domain: a small manufacturer approached by a polished distributor at a trade show
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner balancing a promising partnership with due diligence
exampleSpecs.stakes: one premature purchase order could trap inventory for months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner enjoys the rapport at the booth but waits for references and a test order before granting exclusivity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sample parts arranged under bright trade-show lights

exampleSpecs.domain: a tenant group receiving urgent messages from a supposed building inspector
exampleSpecs.audience: a tenant organizer protecting neighbors without becoming suspicious of everyone
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents might share personal details or miss a real safety notice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:48 p.m., Marit compares the message style with verified city contact channels before forwarding anything to the building list
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone screen glowing in a dim stairwell
mustAvoid: online fraud statistics or crime taxonomy

skillTargets: apply truth bias to ambiguous trust decisions
identify when online signals outrun evidence
evaluate guarded optimism against cynicism and naivete

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one trust decision and split it into two columns: what feels promising and what has been verified. Slow only the unverified part.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
